reasoning: UNSATISFIABLE: If a 9-vertex graph had minimum degree at least 3 and girth at least 7, take any vertex v. It has at least 3 neighbors. Each of those neighbors must have at least 2 additional neighbors besides v. These second-neighborhood vertices must all be distinct; otherwise there would be a triangle or a 4-cycle. Thus the graph would already need at least 1 + 3 + 3*2 = 10 vertices, contradicting that there are only 9 vertices.
